lanes.pitch: Open QR Code, type a web address and download the finished file. It takes a minute, and you need no account and nothing installed.
Lolly opens wearing Lolly Demo, its own sample design system. Give it your colours, fonts and logos once, and every tool wears them from then on.
Lolly runs in a current browser. Install the app when you want it in your dock or app menu, with native file dialogs.
Why it is free, where your files go, how to get the apps and who makes Lolly.
Pick a tool and fill in a few fields, or lay it out yourself on an open canvas. The finished file comes out right either way: colours, fonts and layout are already sorted.
Text that moves, scenes on a timeline, motion that stays on-brand. Cut clips, music and voiceover in Sequence, then export video, GIF or animated SVG.
Record a clean take with live coaching, or turn a voice note into a finished video with Audiogram. No camera, no makeup needed.
Two people, two devices, one design, edited live. Share an invite across the table and both screens hold the same session: there is no server in the middle.
Send it where it was asked for: a link that carries the design, one .lolly file, print-true PDF, video or slides - or straight to Discord, Google Drive and the places you already post.
Playbooks for the teams that make the most files: a seller with a meeting tomorrow, a marketer with forty sizes to fill, a newsroom on deadline and a legal reviewer cleaning a file before it travels.
Bring finished work in, set the rules once, keep the tools you already use.
One render path. The app, the CLI and an agent all make the same file.

Agents are first-class users. Anything a person can make in the app, an agent can make through the MCP server or the CLI: the same tools, the same brand rules, the same render path, and the file still says who made it.

doors.name: Manage
doors.sub: I run it for a team

lanes.pitch: Your organisation runs Lolly Work? Connect the app to its address and sign in. Its tools, design systems and shared projects appear, and your own saves stay yours.
Sign-in with your own identity provider, roles, locked inputs, shared catalogues, approvals and an audit trail, on a Lolly Work server your organisation runs.
A static host is the easy path. Air-gapped is the same install.
The organisation server is open source too. Run it on one machine, on Kubernetes or with your platform team.

Most data exfiltration is mundane: a confidential file handed to a stranger's website for a ten-second job. Lolly's utilities do those jobs inside the app, with no account and no server in the middle, so there is nothing for a data-loss policy to chase.
What stays with you, what each optional service receives, and what Lolly never collects, written out in full.
A file Lolly makes can say who made it and with what. Drop any file on Verify to read its Content Credentials and check them yourself.
